findings.where: Screen 4 (Spread the legs), the sling picture at 360 px light and dark; same at 1280
findings.what: The vertical and sideways parts, the one thing the brief says to see, are only about 25 px at phone width, and at 120° they join into a dashed box round the hook that looks like screen 3's 'freed' outline, because the scale is set for 30° and leaves the top two-thirds of the picture as bare wire; draw the sling larger for the angles shown and keep each leg's two parts visibly apart.

No screen says a leg's vertical part is its pull times sin θ, so the step from 'each vertical part is half the load' to 'tension = half ÷ sin θ' is skipped, and screen 5 asks for the 120° pull before screen 6 gives the 1 ÷ sin θ rule (only the footer caption has it); add that sentence to screen 4 so screen 5 follows from it.

findings.where: Screen 4 (Spread the legs), text plus the line under the picture
findings.what: Screen 4 carries about 114 words (87 above the picture and a 27-word line below that repeats 'its vertical part is still 4.905 kN, half the load'), well over the ~90-word limit; drop the repeat and the 'Each leg pulls the hook down and the load up' opener.

findings.where: Screen 2 (Free the hook), text plus the line under the picture
findings.what: Screen 2 runs to about 99 words because its 23-word line under the picture repeats the text's 'the wire pulls up, each leg pulls down, the three close a triangle'; cut one of them.

The brief promised friction's limit as F = μN and the static-then-sliding drop (with what lubrication does), but the screens give the 300 N limit as a bare example with nothing saying what sets it, and no later lesson picks μ up though lesson 7's belts and clutches will lean on it.

'The leg's strength stays at 8 kN at any angle' calls the leg's safe load its strength, but 8 kN is what it can safely take, not where it breaks; say 'What the leg can safely take stays 8 kN at any angle'.

findings.where: θ label on the sling picture at 120° (screens 5, 6, 8, 9, 12, 13, and screen 4 when spread)
findings.what: At 120° the θ label lands just under the hook, outside its small arc at the lifting point, so it reads as the angle at the hook, the very from-the-vertical slip screen 12 tests; put it inside the wedge at the lifting point or mark θ against a short horizontal line drawn outward from the lifting point.
With its 25-word line under the picture it reaches about 94 words, at the limit, and that line repeats 'the whole load' from the text.
The tiles show the load angle factor and the leg's angle but not each leg's tension, though the screen is about that tension passing the 8 kN mark; show the tension tile.
It says the hook stays still 'so' the pulls add to nothing without the one-line reason that any leftover force would start it moving.

No screen names the general balance rule, that the across parts add to nothing and so do the up parts, which lesson 2 recalls as ΣFx = 0 and ΣFy = 0; screen 13's Why? already uses it, so one sentence there would name it.
The caption 'Each leg's tension is half the weight divided by sin θ…' shows from screen 1, before θ or the sling exists, and hands over screen 5's working; show it from screen 6 on.

findings.where: Lead paragraph above the stepper, every screen
findings.what: The 27-word lead repeats on all 13 screens and pushes each screen's content about four lines down at 360 px; say it once on screen 1.

The opening is a static ring puzzle with a blank band above the ring and an empty right half, and the sling, the thing to be moved, first appears on screen 2, so the opening reads less alive than it could.
The catenary comparison is honest, its 'breaks' is true and it suits an electrician, but in the steps format it never reaches a screen; one line on screen 6 would carry it.
